prompt.context: Our client is BankCoCard, a US credit card subsidiary of the major international bank BankCo. They have a rapidly growing $16 billion dollar credit card portfolio. BankCoCard is interested in lowering their cost of funds for their credit card program by starting an online bank.
prompt.question: BankCoCard would like to know if they should start an online bank and if so, should they launch a savings or a checking account for their new online bank.

clarifying_info.a: BankCoCard wants to launch both a savings and checking account, but their budget only allows for the IT team to build one product this year. Whichever product is not selected will be launched the following year.

clarifying_info.q: How much will it cost to build each product?
clarifying_info.a: The savings and checking accounts are expected to take the same time to build and will cost the same amount to build: $10 million.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current cost of funds?
clarifying_info.a: The current cost of funds is 4% for the credit card portfolio.

clarifying_info.q: Are interest rates expected to change?
clarifying_info.a: Interest rates are not expected to change for the next several years.
Assume all deposits can be lent; no reserves are required.

clarifying_info.q: Will the online bank operate globally?
clarifying_info.a: The online bank will only operate within the US.

exhibits.title: Account Information
exhibits.shows: A table comparing key parameters of the Checking Account and Savings Account side by side.

exhibits.title: New Online Accounts Per Year
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing projected new online checking accounts and new online savings accounts per year from 2018 to 2023, with values on the y-axis in millions.

framework: Define objective: lower cost of funds by capturing cheap deposit funding for the $16B credit card portfolio
Upfront costs: IT build cost ($10M), website/servers, call center infrastructure, hiring and training, marketing and market research, product design
Ongoing revenues by product: Savings = interest income from credit card portfolio; Checking = interest income, overdraft fees, account fees, interchange, ATM fees
Ongoing costs by product: Savings = interest paid to customers, call center, fraud, marketing, statement mailing; Checking = debit card transaction processing, ACH processing, ATM reimbursement
Account-level profitability: lifetime profit per account for savings vs. checking
Market sizing: total lifetime profit of first-year cohort for each product (market size x capture rate x per-account profit)
Recommendation: choose the product that maximizes lifetime profit OR best achieves the stated cost-of-funds objective, and note sequencing for year 2

questions.prompt: Question 1: What upfront costs will there be to launch an online banking product?
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover: infrastructure (servers, website), call center build-out, hiring and training of development and operations team, marketing and market research, and product design. Candidates should structure these into categories (technology, people, marketing).

questions.prompt: Question 2: What are the ongoing revenues and costs of a savings account? What additional revenues and costs does a checking account have?
questions.guidance: Savings revenues: interest income from lending deposits to the credit card portfolio. Savings costs: interest paid to customers, call center, fraud losses, marketing, statement mailing. Checking additional revenues: overdraft fees, account fees, interchange income, ATM fees. Checking additional costs: debit card transaction processing, ACH transaction processing, ATM reimbursement.

questions.prompt: Question 3: What are possible ways of acquiring new accounts for online banking products? (Interviewer should keep asking for more until the candidate has identified at least 4.)
questions.guidance: Strong answers include: online advertisements, search engine optimization, partnerships, affiliate marketing, cross-selling current credit card customers, billboards, sponsoring events, tabling at major events.

questions.prompt: Question 4: The online bank will lend the deposits to the credit card portfolio at a 3% annual interest rate. What is the lifetime profit of a single checking account versus a savings account?
questions.guidance: Candidate should set up revenue and cost streams over the account lifetime using Exhibit 1 data. A strong candidate will ask about discounting future cash flows / discount rate (interviewer tells them it is not necessary). Should correctly identify overdraft fee as a probabilistic revenue item.

math.setup: Use Exhibit 1 data. Savings life = 5 years, Checking life = 10 years. No discounting required.
math.answer: Savings account lifetime profit per account = $110; Checking account lifetime profit per account = $280

questions.prompt: Question 5: Calculate the total lifetime profit of all accounts opened in the first year for both the savings and checking products. BankCo expects to capture 10% of the market for online accounts of whichever product they launch. After calculating, are you suspicious of any of the assumptions or data?
questions.guidance: Candidate reads the 2018 starting market size from Exhibit 2 (savings = 20M new accounts, checking = 15M), applies 10% capture rate, multiplies by per-account profit. After the calculation, a strong candidate questions aggressive assumptions such as capturing 10% of the market in year 1, average deposit balances, account life assumptions, acquisition cost estimates, or growth rate projections.

math.setup: Use 2018 base year new accounts from Exhibit 2 and 10% market capture assumption.
math.answer: Total lifetime profit for savings accounts opened in year 1 = $220M; for checking accounts = $420M

brainstorming.prompt: What are the ongoing revenues and costs of a savings account, and what additional revenues and costs does a checking account have compared to savings?

categories.name: Savings Revenues
ideas: Interest income from lending deposits to the credit card portfolio at 3%

categories.name: Savings Costs
ideas: Interest paid to customers (2% on deposits)

recommendation: BankCoCard should start an online bank, launching the checking account in the first year and the savings account in the following year

Launch the checking account first because it generates nearly twice the lifetime profit per account ($280 vs. $110) and nearly twice the total lifetime profit for the first-year cohort ($420M vs. $220M)
The online checking account market is growing faster than the savings market (estimated CAGR ~20% vs. ~10% based on Exhibit 2 projections)

Bonus insight: A candidate recalling the original cost-of-funds objective would note that savings accounts generate far more deposits per account ($5,000 vs. $2,000), meaning 2M savings accounts yield ~$10B in deposits versus ~$3B for 1.5M checking accounts — which better addresses the stated goal of lowering the cost of funds for the $16B credit card portfolio, creating a nuanced case for prioritizing savings instead
risks: BankCoCard may capture less than 10% of the market
Reputation risk if the online bank launch is poorly executed
Account acquisition costs could be higher than projected
Product may not be sufficiently differentiated from established competitors
Regulatory risk associated with launching an online bank
next_steps: Meet with regulators to understand online banking licensing requirements
Survey potential customers to inform product design
Collect industry reports to validate market size and growth assumptions
Host focus groups for product testing
Begin hiring IT staff and operations team
Design the website and digital infrastructure
Request additional budget to fund both products across two years
Build or outsource the call center
